raccoon-removal.extendedBody:
Signs You Have Raccoons in Your McDonough Home

  • Heavy thumping or scratching in the attic at night — slow and heavy at dusk or dawn is the classic raccoon signature; faster, lighter movement is usually squirrels.
  • Chittering or trilling vocalizations from above the ceiling — kits begin vocalizing at 2-3 weeks old and grow steadily louder through 8 weeks.
  • Torn soffits, lifted shingles, bent attic-fan housings, pulled fascia, or pried ridge vents — raccoons are by far the strongest residential intruder and will physically lever entry points open.
  • Large segmented droppings (around 3 inches, blunt-ended) in the attic or on the roofline — raccoon scat carries Baylisascaris procyonis (raccoon roundworm) eggs that remain infectious for years; do not disturb without PPE.
  • Knocked-over garbage cans, overturned bird feeders, or koi-pond raids — McDonough subdivision-edge properties absorb constant food-driven foraging pressure.
  • Daytime sightings of a raccoon acting disoriented, aggressive, or unsteady — possible rabies indicator. Don't approach, keep pets and kids indoors, and call for same-day removal.

Raccoon in Your House Right Now? What to Do

If a raccoon has made it into the living space — not just the attic — call for same-day McDonough dispatch first. While you wait:

  • Confine the raccoon to one room. Close interior doors and block the gap at the bottom of the door with a rolled towel.
  • If safe, open one exterior door or window in that room. An adult raccoon will usually leave on its own when given an obvious exit — turn interior lights off, leave exterior lights on, keep pets and people clear.
  • Don't corner, swat at, or try to grab the raccoon. Any direct contact is treated as potential rabies exposure under Georgia DPH guidance — even with no visible bite.
  • Keep pets out of the area entirely. Dogs in particular tangle with raccoons and lose, and the vet workup that follows is expensive and unpleasant.
  • If your pet or a family member made contact, call Henry County Animal Control and your physician or vet immediately — rabies post-exposure prophylaxis is time-sensitive.

How Raccoons Get Into McDonough Homes

Most McDonough property is 1990s-2020s subdivision construction, and the entry-point profile follows builder-grade material aging:

  • Vinyl-soffit corner separations at fascia-meet points — the most common 1990s-2010s subdivision entry; the panel pulls loose at a corner and a raccoon levers it open from there.
  • Lifted ridge-vent flashing on aged shingled roofs — raccoons work loose flashing into a usable opening over a few nights.
  • Chimney chase cap failures — builder-grade galvanized chase caps rust through at the seam by year 20-25 and become open chimney access. Female raccoons take advantage every spring.
  • Bent attic-fan housings and gable-vent screens aged through — both are quick entries once the underlying material fatigues.
  • Uncapped masonry chimneys in McDonough's small pre-1900 historic-downtown core around the Henry County Courthouse square — a small but real subset of jobs; these are classic raccoon maternity dens because the chimney box is dark, warm, and predator-free.

Raccoon Health Risks Around Your Family

Raccoons aren't aggressive by default, but they are a documented disease vector — and the risk is the reason raccoon removal and decontamination are professional-grade work, not a DIY job:

  • Rabies. Raccoons are one of three primary terrestrial rabies reservoirs in Georgia (alongside foxes and skunks). Any direct contact — bite, scratch, or saliva on broken skin — triggers post-exposure prophylaxis decisions.
  • Baylisascaris procyonis (raccoon roundworm). Eggs are shed in scat and stay infectious in attic insulation, soil, and on contaminated surfaces for years. Larval migration in humans can cause serious neurological damage. Attic remediation uses HEPA equipment and PPE for a reason.
  • Leptospirosis. Transmitted through urine to people and (more commonly) to pets, particularly dogs. Worth flagging to your vet if your dog has had outdoor exposure during raccoon activity.
  • Canine distemper. Not transmissible to people, but devastating to unvaccinated dogs. A raccoon visibly stumbling in daylight is more likely to have distemper than rabies, but the live-animal handling protocol is the same: don't approach, call for removal.

The McDonough Raccoon Removal Process

Durable resolution is exclusion-based, not trap-only:

  • Free on-site inspection — every viable entry point mapped (most McDonough properties show 2-4), kit presence confirmed, and any structural damage scoped for repair. No charge if you don't authorize the job.
  • Kit-aware eviction or humane trapping — during the February-April denning window, kits are located and removed by hand so the family stays intact; outside denning season, one-way exclusion doors let the adult leave on its own and prevent re-entry.
  • Structural exclusion — every entry point sealed with galvanized steel mesh, hardware cloth, or material-matched repair. Soffit panels reseated, ridge-vent flashing replaced, custom-fabricated stainless-steel chimney caps installed where needed.
  • Attic decontamination — HEPA-equipped removal of contaminated insulation, enzymatic sanitization, and a Baylisascaris roundworm protocol when scat load warrants. Documented for insurance claims.
  • 1-year exclusion warranty on full-scope work — if a raccoon gets back in through a sealed entry point within 12 months, the rework is on the contractor.

The contractor serving McDonough is local to Henry County — same-day arrival is the standard scope for McDonough addresses, with 24/7 emergency dispatch for live-raccoon-in-living-space, attic kits, chimney falls, and pet-exposure situations.
